papers.title_in_file: Optimal storage capacity of quantum Hopfield neural networks
papers.version_note: arXiv:2210.07894v1 (14 Oct 2022) with the Supplemental Material appended in the same text; the text is the paper the record names.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that generalizes Gardner's program to open quantum Hopfield networks and computes the maximal storage capacity of a driven-dissipative spin-1/2 associative memory by replica methods.

existing.note: The decrease is reported for a fixed minimal overlap (m = 0.95 in the map shown) and rests on the mean-field, high-overlap and extremely diluted network approximations of the derivation; the stored value omits these conditions. The paper does not state a monotonicity proof, it reports the numerical result.
existing.value: The authors report that, in the map computed for a fixed minimal overlap m = 0.95 and under the approximations of their derivation, the maximal storage capacity of the open-system quantum associative memory decreases monotonically upon increasing both temperature and coherent drive, which they say indicates that both quantities introduce noise with respect to the pattern retrieval capability.
quotes: We ﬁnd that the maximal storage capacity decreases monotonically upon increasing both temperature and coherent drive
which indicates that both quantities introduce noise
for a ﬁxed minimal overlap m = 0.95
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical, numerical result from one model; not upgraded.

existing.note: The abstract states the method and its derivation route. Note the derivation is carried out with mean-field, high-overlap and extremely diluted network approximations (see new assertions).
quotes: we propose and explore a general method for evaluating the maximal storage capacity of quantum neural network models
we exploit the theory of classical spin glasses for deriving the optimal storage capacity of quantum networks with quenched pattern variables
existing.certainty_reason: The abstract states what the paper proposes.

existing.note: The statement is made in the Introduction with references [35-37]; it is cited, not tested here.
quotes: applications to speciﬁc models do not provide conclusive results with regard to enhanced quantum storage advantage [35–37]
existing.certainty_reason: A claim the paper makes about other work.

assertions.value: The authors define the storage capacity as alpha equal to p over N, quantifying the number p of patterns that can be stored in a network of N constituents.
quotes: the storage capacity, α ≡ p N , quantifying the number p of patterns that can be stored in a network of N constituents

assertions.value: The authors state that with Hebb's prescription and random patterns the neural network can store on the order of 0.138N memories, citing earlier work.
quotes: the NN can store on the order of 0.138N memories [27]
assertions.reader_inference: This is the classical Amit-Gutfreund-Sompolinsky value, quoted for context.

assertions.value: The authors describe Gardner's program as requiring a set of patterns to be stationary solutions of the dynamics while the learning rule is left as a free parameter, with the typical volume of parameter space fulfilling the retrieval condition as the quantity of interest.
quotes: consists in requiring a set of patterns to be stationary solutions of the dynamics, while the learning rule is left as free parameter
The quantity of interest is the typical volume of parameter space fulﬁlling the condition of retrieval.

assertions.value: The authors state that recent findings, combining Gardner's program with the framework of quantum maps, formally show the possibility of a quantum advantage in the storage capacity of quantum neural networks over their classical counterparts.
quotes: recent ﬁndings formally show the possibility of a quantum advantage in the storage capacity of quantum NNs over their classical counterparts

assertions.value: The authors state that, in the spirit of Gardner's program, they require the quantum dynamical evolutions to display a number of stationary solutions, or stable quantum memories, without specifying any learning rule, and that the typical fractional volume of such evolutions represents a generalized partition function, which maps the capacity evaluation to a classical statistical mechanics model.
quotes: we require the quantum dynamical evolutions to display a number of stationary solutions, or stable quantum memories, without specifying any learning rule
represents a generalized partition function
This enables us to map the evaluation of the optimal storage capacity of a quantum NN to a classical statistical mechanics model.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Introduction states the paper's own construction.

assertions.value: The authors state that the point at which the typical volume vanishes signals that the maximal capacity has been reached.
quotes: The point of a vanishing volume signals that αc has been reached
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the method section as the criterion for the maximal capacity.

assertions.value: The authors state that the model is an open quantum spin-based associative memory introduced in earlier work, and that the system undergoes a Markovian time evolution in which a dissipative retrieval dynamics competes with a coherent quantum dynamics.
quotes: The system undergoes a Markovian time evolution resulting from a dissipative retrieval dynamics that competes with a coherent quantum dynamics.
introduced in Refs. [24, 25], and analyzed in the limit of vanishing
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract and Introduction describe the model studied.

quotes: which can lead the system into one
whereas the quantum drive

assertions.value: The authors state that the closed equations of motion for the overlap operators are derived by applying approximations, including a mean field approximation, a regime of high overlap along the z-direction, a homogeneous distribution of the misalignment between patterns and spins, and a spatial homogeneity approximation of the local energy.
assertions.anchor: Dynamics of macroscopic overlap operators, p.3; Supplement I, p.9
quotes: A ﬁnite set of closed equations of motion (EoMs) for the overlap operators
we employ (i) a mean ﬁeld approximation
we further employ a homogeneity approximation with respect to the site dependency of the local energy
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the approximations on which its equations rest.
assertions.reader_inference: The capacity results therefore hold within these approximations only.

assertions.value: The authors state that they continue to work in the low quantum drive regime, and claim that for larger quantum drive stability would still be ensured by the previous argument.
quotes: In the following, we continue to work in the low quantum drive regime, stressing that for larger quantum drive stability would still be ensured by the previous argument.
assertions.certainty_reason: Supplement II.A states the regime the calculation is done in.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the classical limit the stability condition is fulfilled for the overlap above about 0.4478, which is already guaranteed by their approximation of large overlap.
quotes: This condition is fulﬁlled for Mzµ ≳ 0.4478
which is already guaranteed by our approximation of large overlap

assertions.value: The authors state that the pattern average is difficult for non-Gaussian pattern distributions, so they assume an extremely diluted network with a finite number C of matrix elements per spin, with C below the logarithm of N.
assertions.anchor: Storage capacity section, p.4; Supplement II.B, p.12
quotes: This average is diﬃcult to perform for non-Gaussian pat
we assume to deal with an extremely diluted network [33, 43]
We further choose C < log(N ), which is referred to as logarithmic dilution
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the dilution assumption on which the replica calculation depends.
assertions.reader_inference: The capacity is computed for a diluted network; the paper does not say how it carries over to a dense one.

assertions.value: The authors state that it can be shown, citing earlier work, that only cumulants up to order 2 are finite in the thermodynamic limit for the diluted networks, so that the pattern average of the replicated volume reduces to the second cumulant.
quotes: It can be shown that only cumulants up to order 2 are ﬁnite in the TDL for the diluted networks [43].

assertions.value: The authors state that they assume replica symmetry and site symmetry for the saddle-point solutions, as in the classical treatment, and that the capacity is reached in the limit of maximal replica correlation q to 1.
assertions.anchor: Storage capacity section, p.4; Supplement II.B, p.14
quotes: we assume replica symmetry and a site symmetry to be fulﬁlled as in the classical treatment [33]
The maximal capacity αc(m, T, Ω) is reached in the limit of maximal replica correlation q → 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated assumptions of the replica calculation.
assertions.reader_inference: No replica-symmetry-breaking check is reported; the paper reports none.

assertions.value: The authors state that they replace the step functions by the number of solutions, following an assumption from earlier work that the number of solutions approaches zero as the capacity approaches its maximum, and that the number of solutions factorizes over sites under a homogeneity assumption.
quotes: following the assumption [33] that the number of solutions
Nµ factorizes over the sites

assertions.value: The authors state that they will find the maximal capacity to be strictly decreasing with the z overlap, so that the saddle-point value of the overlap is the lower bound m, and they therefore replace the overlap by m.
quotes: the saddle-point value for Mz is given by the lower bound m

assertions.value: The authors state that the maximal capacity is computed numerically from a self-consistent set of algebraic and integral saddle-point equations, using a modified Newton method with fixed-point iteration for the y overlap.
quotes: The maximal capacity αc can be calculated numerically
This is done by a modiﬁed Newton method

assertions.value: The authors report that in the classical limit at zero temperature the numerical result reproduces the classical result derived by Gardner.
quotes: In the classical limit Ω = 0, at vanishing temperature we consistently obtain the classical result originally derived by Gardner
we derive the limit obtained by Gardner
assertions.reader_inference: The value 2 itself is printed in a garbled formula in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors report that the figure maps the maximal storage capacity over temperature and quantum drive for a fixed minimal overlap m = 0.95, and shows projections of the maximal Hamiltonian drive of non-vanishing storage capacity for minimal overlaps m = 0.95, 0.93 and 0.9.
quotes: Map of the maximal storage capacity αc in the parameter space of temperature and quantum drive (T, Ω) for a ﬁxed minimal overlap m = 0.95.

assertions.value: The authors report that for any fixed temperature there exists a critical value of the Hamiltonian drive at which a discontinuous crossover from a finite to zero maximal storage capacity takes place.
quotes: there exists a critical value, Ωc(T ), at which a discontinuous crossover from a ﬁnite to zero max

assertions.value: The authors report that for large temperatures the maximal capacity decays as beta squared with beta the inverse temperature, and, in the supplement, that this is a quadratic decay of the maximal capacity at large temperature.
quotes: temperatures, the maximal capacity decreases as αc ∼ β2
which shows a quadratic decay of the maximal capacity at large temperature

assertions.value: The authors state that a first-order expansion in the inverse temperature sets a maximal value for the Hamiltonian drive up to which a solution can still be found.
quotes: which sets a maximal value for the Hamiltonian drive up to which a solution can still be found
assertions.reader_inference: The closed form of the critical drive is garbled in the text layer, so it is not entered.

assertions.value: The authors report that for small Hamiltonian drive the first-order contribution to h(t) vanishes, and that the effect of the Hamiltonian drive on the maximal storage capacity is quadratic in the drive.
quotes: As a consequence, the ﬁrst order contribution in Ω to h(t) vanishes
In conclusion, this shows that the eﬀect of the Hamiltonian drive to the maximal storage capacity is quadratic in Ω.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement is a perturbative argument under the paper's approximations; it is not entered as a theorem because the paper names none.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quadratic behaviour is confirmed by the results they find from numerically solving the system dynamics.
quotes: This behaviour is conﬁrmed by the results we ﬁnd from numerically solving the system dynamics.
assertions.reader_inference: No data for this confirmation is shown in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that they establish for the first time that robust storage of an extensive number of patterns is possible under Hamiltonian perturbations, and that they have thus established the robustness of storage capability upon perturbing the retrieval mechanism via a Hamiltonian drive.
quotes: We establish for the ﬁrst time that robust storage of an extensive number of patterns is possible under Hamiltonian perturbations
We have thus established the robustness of
assertions.reader_inference: The robustness is shown only within the paper's approximations, for one model.

assertions.value: The authors state that their technique is applicable to a wider class of quantum associative memories, and that the method could be used to study other quantum neural network models, some of them potentially revealing a quantum advantage, or to select optimal parameters for storage capacity.
quotes: is applicable to a wider class of quantum associative memories [22, 35, 38]
some of them potentially revealing a quantum advantage
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports a capacity reduction from the drive, not an advantage, for its own model.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is a challenging open problem to analyze quantum associative memories with an extensive number of patterns and to determine the maximal number of patterns the networks can reliably store.
quotes: It is a challenging open problem to analyze quantum associative memories with an extensive number of patterns
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the open problem the paper addresses.

assertions.value: The authors state that it will be interesting to identify quantum neural networks that allow storage of quantum-mechanical patterns and to assess their maximum storage capacity, and note that the model studied stores classical binary patterns.
assertions.anchor: Conclusions and outlook, p.5; Open Quantum Hopfield Model, p.3
quotes: It will be interesting to identify QNNs that allow for storage of quantum-mechanical patterns and assess their maximum storage capacity
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusions name this as not yet done.
assertions.reader_inference: The patterns in this model are classical binary configurations, so the quantum-pattern case is outside the results.
